title: Even villagers who don't write picked the round shape for 'bouba'
hook: Spiky is kiki, round is bouba. A Himba village in Namibia gave the same answer

open.title: The researchers who carried a spiky shape and a round shape to a village in Namibia
open.line: One spiky star, one wobbly flower. One is bouba, the other is kiki.

summary: Most people call the round shape bouba. The Himba of Namibia, who don't write, did too, but matched taste to shape differently from Westerners.

text: One spiky star, one wobbly flower.
One is bouba, the other is kiki.

panels.text: The spiky one's kiki. Why even ask?

text: A 2001 paper wrote that 95% of people pick the spiky one as kiki.
Even with shapes they've never seen, called just a Martian word.
Actually, some argued it was down to the letters.
B looks round and K looks spiky.
So in 2013 a British team went to Himba villages in northern Namibia.
They don't write, and Western culture barely reaches them.
28 of 34 Himba people picked the round one as bouba.
Without letters, the answer was the same.

panels.text: So everyone's brain works the same?

text: Westerners match sparkling water to the spiky shape. The Himba didn't.
Westerners match bitter chocolate to the spiky one. The Himba more often matched milder milk chocolate to it.

sources: Ramachandran & Hubbard (2001), Synaesthesia: A Window Into Perception, Thought and Language, Journal of Consciousness Studies 8(12)
Bremner et al. (2013), Bouba and Kiki in Namibia?, Cognition 126(2)
Ćwiek et al. (2022), The bouba/kiki effect is robust across cultures and writing systems, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B
